investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity (resource exhaustion or quota limit reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~135–145 seconds, the eval runner timed out before the agent reached a ready state, leaving all required evidence fields empty and causing the contract validation to fail on all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents swarm runtime in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T15:57–16:02Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the required peer-pod VM because 2 nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity were fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, and the remote-agent-state probe produced zero evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the two eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) to provision a remote agent pod, the scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and the pod remained Unschedulable for ~145 seconds before the check timed out. No agent was ever created, so the state-polling step that would have produced orgId, agentId, readyState, and state evidence was never reached. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-level failure reflecting the inability to provision a new remote agent VM at the time of the run.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already small and any VM slot exhaustion on those 2 nodes causes a total scheduling failure.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity (resource exhaustion or quota limit reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~135–145 seconds, the eval runner timed out before the agent reached a ready state, leaving all required evidence fields empty and causing the contract validation to fail on all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents swarm runtime in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T16:00–16:02Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod remained unscheduled for 144 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every required-evidence assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" confirms no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot recover it. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completed, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
